clinician.final_diagnosis: pulmonary nocardiosis was retained on the bacteriological study of the pleural fluid after a direct examination and a positive culture.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 54-year-old farmer with a 46 pack-year smoking history presented with productive cough, hemoptysis, altered general condition, and feverish feelings. Clinical exam showed polypnea, hypoxemia, and dullness of the left hemithorax. Initial chest X-ray revealed a hydro-pneumothorax, and a CT scan showed a left lung abscess communicating with bronchi, left pyopneumothorax, and right peribronchovascular micronodules. Pleural puncture yielded chocolate-colored purulent fluid. Direct examination of the pleural fluid showed numerous filamentous gram-positive bacilli, initially evoking actinomyces. Culture of the pleural fluid, after prolonged incubation, isolated bacterial strains with colony morphology 'in favor of Nocardia'. Gram staining and modified Kinyoun staining confirmed the presumptive identification of Nocardia genus and ruled out Actinomyces. Specific Nocardia species identification and antibiotic sensitivity testing were not performed due to technical limitations. Tuberculosis was ruled out by negative BK and GeneXpert MTB/RIF in pleural fluid and sputum. Initial treatment with Amoxicillin + clavulanic acid led to clinical, biological, and radiological improvement after 2 weeks.
